Village, Krishnarajapura Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk.
 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing, In
B-Group, This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following relief:
a) Issue a Writ of Mandamus or such directions for 2nd respondent /Bengaluru Development Authority to consider the representation dated 10.04.2014 vide Annexure-A for incorporation of its name in the concerned records with respect to claiming compensation/TDR for road widening in sy.No.97/1 measuring 13 guntas and Sy.no.97/2 measuring 2 guntas (total15 guntas) of Hagaduru village,
Krishnarajapura Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk.

2. Sri Harish H.V., learned counsel for petitioner submitted that Director of Petitioner - Company had entered into registered agreement of sale on 06.02.2013 with owners of lands bearing Sy.nos.97/1 and 97/2 to extent of 22 guntas and 01 acre 09 guntas respectively of Hagaduru village,
Krishnarajapura Hobli, Bengaluru.

Since out of same, extent of 13 guntas in Sy.no.97/1 and 02 guntas in Sy.no.97/2, totally measuring 15 guntas was acquired for formation of Peripheral NC:
2023:KHC:39743 Ring Road, registered sale deed was executed on 25.02.2014 in respect of remaining extent in favour of petitioner.
In said sale deed, vendors had also agreed and transferred their rights to collect TDR or compensation from BDA, in respect of 15 guntas of land acquired for Peripheral Ring Road.

And when petitioner submitted representation at Annexure-A on 10.04.2014 claiming compensation/TDR in respect of land acquired, it remained without consideration,
constraining to file this writ petition.

Since right to receive compensation was legal right, denial despite demand by submitting representation was unjustified, therefore, learned counsel sought for allowing writ petition.

sentences.text: On other hand, Sri Ajay Kumar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 would submit that since acquisition of land for Peripheral Ring Road was prior to execution of agreement of sale / sale deed, petitioner as purchaser would at best be entitled for compensation.

Therefore, relief sought by petitioner in representation i.e., to incorporate its name in records for future communication etc.,
not yet matured since process of passing award also not yet begun.
It was submitted that as and when said process would begin, petitioner's claim NC: 2023:KHC:39743 would be taken into consideration and notice would be issued to petitioner.

4. Heard learned counsel and writ petition record.
5.
Admittedly, petitioner is seeking for direction to respondents to consider its representation.
And respondents have stated that same would be considered at appropriate stage in accordance with law after issuing notice to petitioner.

6. In view of above, writ petition is disposed of directing respondents no.2 and 3 to issue notice to petitioner as an interested person at time of passing award, consider representation at Annexure-A,
along with such other material he may produce and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

Needless to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law.
Sd/-
JUDGE Psg*
